title: Inharmonic Wavetable Synthesis — rich
forward_vector: I am the manifest of Inharmonic Wavetable Synthesis's rich face: three walks that each test a claim the page makes — the flat line, the settling piano, the unison bundle — and the project's own instruments, renders and measurements laid beside the sections they prove, with the fingerprint of the words each piece was made against. I grow when the entry is enriched again; I never hold the entry's words.

pieces.file: Inharmonic Wavetable Synthesis — rich — bend the line.html
pieces.title: bend the flat line · a walk in five steps
pieces.caption: **The flat line, measured.** It opens where Three Kinds of Warp ends: a one-cycle table can only put energy on the harmonic lines. The same tone rebuilt as a bank of sines plays the table back to within 2 × 10⁻¹³ of its peak, and the share of energy between the lines stays at zero. Bend one partial and only that one leaves the grid. Then draw any curve; at depth 0 every line goes home. Last, the curves the page names are set beside curves measured from real materials. The piano strings sit on the stiff-string bow to within 0.8 to 5.3 cents rms. The bell sits on neither the bow nor the Bessel positions.
pieces.near: Any deviation from that flat line introduces inharmonicity

pieces.title: bending the line · the May proof
pieces.caption: 36 partials while the stiffness B sweeps from 0 to 0.005 over 12 s, at four moments. The faint grid is the harmonic series; the peaks walk off it to the right, further the higher they go.
pieces.near: This is the shape of piano string inharmonicity

pieces.file: Inharmonic Wavetable Synthesis — rich — two ways to settle.html
pieces.title: two ways to settle · a walk in five steps
pieces.caption: **The settling piano, beside a real one.** A measured piano A2: its loudness wall alone, then its own bend, then the two pulled apart, then the page's recipe, then both on one chart. The string's stiffness holds within 3 % over 8 s. The bend you hear (power-weighted, so mostly partials 2 and 3) settles twice: in the first 0.09 s partials 2 and 3 move a few cents, which may be the string or the tracker's first frames; after that the line holds and the loudness wall carries the slow fall, 1.83 to 1.34 cents by 2.6 s. The recipe at B = 0.002, set at this string's pitch, starts 8 times higher, with partial 20 509 cents sharp, and relaxes to zero by 0.5 s.

pieces.title: the recipe, on the organ wall · 8.5 s
pieces.caption: Three strikes at three organ timbres, each wearing June's designed piano trajectory, whose stiffness eases from attack to rest, at depth 0.3. This is the page's settling gesture, not the measured string. Rendered by the steward, 2026-10-14.

pieces.title: a bell dissolving into harmony · 6 s

pieces.title: two clocks, a chord · 18 s
pieces.caption: An A major chord. τ_A creeps across the organ table while τ_B and the depth knob ride two slow LFOs of their own, so the shape and the bend drift out of step. Rendered by the steward, 2026-10-14.

pieces.file: Inharmonic Wavetable Synthesis — rich — the bundle of lines.html
pieces.title: the bundle of lines · a walk in five steps
pieces.caption: **Steep or high?** One voice; two detuned the ordinary way, whose beating already grows as n; two spread along τ_B, where partial 1 stays still and the gap opens to the right; a bundle on the bow, the Bessel positions or a measured string; and last the section's reason put to the test. When the frames relax a shape, voices δ apart differ by δ times its height, so the Bessel bundle is widest at partial 32, where the curve is flattest. The measured string's frames barely change, so its bundle barely fans. The width is δ times the height only because these trajectories relax as a whole, by uniform scaling; in general it follows how fast each partial's place changes along τ_B.
pieces.near: This is exactly the behavior of a real string ensemble playing unison

offers.what: The settling piano is a designed gesture, not what a piano does. Measured (trajectory-library/piano-A2.wtb.json; the two-ways-to-settle piece; the challenge record): the A2 string's fitted stiffness moves 8.32 → 8.05 × 10⁻⁵ over 8 s (−3.2 %), and partial 32 sits at 71.1 cents at 0.03 s and 71.0 at 0.59 s. Its heard bend (power-weighted |cents|) settles twice, on two time scales. In the first 0.09 s it falls 4.67 → 1.83 cents, and that is partials 2 and 3 moving from +3.6 and −6.1 cents to within 2 (with levels frozen at the strike, 4.67 → 2.00); whether that is the string or the tracker's first frames is unsettled. After that the line holds and the loudness wall carries the fall, as the steward's proposal of 2026-10-14 (scroll, steward-018) says: at A2, 1.83 → 1.34 cents by 2.6 s with the frozen line near 1.7–2.0; at A1, 2.66 → 1.71 cents between 3.8 and 5.5 s while the frozen line holds at 2.9–3.3. Suggest the paragraph say a real string's bend holds steady while its loudness wall dims, and that a bend relaxing to flat over 500 ms is a designed gesture no string makes. The same holds for § The Architecture's 'exactly as a piano note does', in its paragraph on frames as temporal evolution.

'Piano (Bass) — strong upward bow, B ≈ 0.001–0.002, settling over ~200ms' is too stiff and does not settle. On the one sampled concert grand in the library (Ableton Core Library), B = 4.67 × 10⁻⁵ at A1 and 8.30 × 10⁻⁵ at A2, 42.8 and 12.0 times below the page's range, about 3× an octave above A2, and 2.3 × 10⁻³ only at A5 (885 Hz) (keyboard-stiffness.png). Published bass values are about 2 × 10⁻⁴ (Hinrichsen, arXiv 1203.5101), so the page's range sits at or above the published top for bass, and this grand sits 2–4× below even that. B moves −3.2 % at A2, +1.7 % at A1, +5.6 % at A4, and +11.5 % at A3: nowhere a settling. The same 0.002 is the settling piano's 'B ≈ 0.002 at partial 20': it puts partial 20 509 cents sharp at any pitch, against 28 cents on the measured A2 string. Suggest the list carry the measured values with the instrument named, the published range beside them, and drop 'settling', and 'Piano (Treble) … faster settling' with it. The steward proposed the bass correction on 2026-10-14 (scroll, steward-018).

offers.section: The Cube Architecture: Higher-Dimensional Framing, Unison, and Spatial Partials
offers.what: Two things in the unison paragraph don't hold as written. (1) 'Bessel spacings … shallow near partial 1 and steepens toward higher partials' is the reverse of the Bessel shape: in cents off each harmonic it jumps 238.5 between partials 1 and 2, then 76.4, and only 0.44 between 31 and 32, levelling toward 1200·log₂(π / 2.4048) = 462.7 cents. (2) The braid and the fan follow the curve's height, not its slope: when frames relax a shape S toward flat, two voices δ apart along τ_B differ by δ·Sₙ. Measured in the bundle piece with three voices at δ = 0.08, the Bessel bundle is widest at partial 32 (71.9 cents), where the curve is flattest, and already 38.2 cents wide at partial 2. For the stiff-string bow, height and slope rise together, so its braid-then-fan holds (partial 1 0.03 cents, partial 32 23.8 cents, two voices). This holds exactly because the frames relax as a whole; in general the width follows how fast each partial's place changes along τ_B. Suggest 'the curve is nearly flat there' → 'the curve's place barely changes along τ_B there (for a shape that relaxes as a whole, where it is near zero)', and that the Bessel shape braids only at partial 1.

offers.section: The Cube Architecture: Higher-Dimensional Framing, Unison, and Spatial Partials
offers.what: 'This is exactly the behavior of a real string ensemble … The physical accuracy emerges geometrically from the curve's shape.' A plain detune already makes the upper partials beat faster: two voices 4 cents apart beat at 0.254 Hz × n on a flat line at 110 Hz, exactly as n (the piece shows n^1.05 only because its base voice sits on a bow). What spreading along τ_B adds is a still fundamental (0.002 Hz) and a much steeper rise, about n³ on the bow (measured n^2.98). A real ensemble's players differ in pitch, so its fundamentals beat too. And the library's measured trajectories give almost no bundle: the A2 string's frames differ by 0.07 cents at partial 32 at δ = 0.08, against 11.3 cents for a designed relaxing bow at the same B. Suggest the sentence say τ_B spread is a designed shimmer that locks the fundamental, and that a real ensemble's detune beats at every partial.

'A step-function pattern locating partials at Bessel function zeros gives bell and cymbal inharmonicity', and the Cross-Domain line on Bessel Functions in Synthesis ('circular membranes — drum, bell, cymbal'), are model claims that don't hold. The zeros of J₀ are the axisymmetric modes of an ideal circular membrane clamped at its rim, a drum head (and only that subset; the full membrane interleaves its m ≥ 1 modes). A bell is a shell and a cymbal a plate; neither follows a J₀ zero series. The measured Brooklyn bell (rank-filed, 24 modes) runs 1, 1.135, 1.451, 2.178 against J₀'s 1, 2.295, 3.598, 1621 cents rms from the J₀ shape; the four piano strings sit 0.8 to 5.3 cents rms from their bow. Suggest naming the J₀ shape a membrane or drum-head shape in those two sentences only. The alien bell choir's 'sounds bell-like in character' is a perceptual metaphor, and stays. The ratios the page quotes (1.0, 2.29, 3.60, 4.90) are right for J₀ (2.2954, 3.5985, 4.9033).

'B' names two things. It is the depth knob (§ The B Depth Scalar; fₙ = n · f₀ · 2^(B · Δfₙ / 1200); 'B=0 bypasses Wavetable B'; 'B=1.5' in § What This Sounds Like). It is also the string's stiffness coefficient (§ Wavetable B's 'the B coefficient formula'; 'B ≈ 0.002 at partial 20'; 'B ≈ 0.001–0.002' in § Physical Trajectory Library; f_n = n·f₀·√(1+B·n²) in § Cross-Domain Resonance). The plugin already calls the depth knob Bend, and the pieces here call it D. Suggest renaming the depth scalar wherever it means depth, B Depth → Bend depth, and leaving B for stiffness.
